build-question.prompt: We deploy our Next.js app to the 4 GB production server. Can I just run npm run build on the box to save time? Two short lines.

claude_code_with_recall.result:
No. Your team's notes say `npm run build` runs out of memory on the 4 GB box and takes the live app down with it.
Build on your laptop or in CI, ship the standalone output, and have the server just switch the symlink and restart.

claude_code_without_recall.result:
You can, but `next build` often needs 1–3+ GB of RAM. On a 4 GB box that's also serving the live app, it can run out of memory, get killed, or slow down production while it runs.

It's safer to build in CI or on your machine with `output: 'standalone'` and copy the build to the server; if you must build on the box, add swap and cap Node's memory with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048`.

oauth-question.prompt: Our Gmail sync started failing with 403 insufficientPermissions right after we added the Calendar scope. Re-running the login didn't help. What's going on and what should I do? Answer in at most 4 short lines.

claude_code_with_recall.result:
Your existing token was issued before the Calendar scope existed, and re-running login just hands back that cached token, so Google rejects calls that need the new scope.
Fix: delete every stored copy of the token (token.json, DB row, localStorage), then run consent once with `prompt=consent` and request **all** scopes, the Gmail ones and Calendar together.
Before retrying the sync, check that `getTokenInfo(accessToken)` lists the Calendar scope.
This comes from your team's note `vault/google-oauth-new-scope-needs-reconsent.md`; I haven't looked at your auth code.

claude_code_without_recall.result:
Your app is most likely still using the old refresh token, which only carries the original Gmail scopes. Google often skips the consent screen when you log in again, so no new grant gets issued. It's also possible that adding Calendar replaced the Gmail scope in your scope list instead of adding to it.
To fix it, delete the stored token and revoke the app's access at myaccount.google.com/permissions. Then request the Gmail and Calendar scopes together, with `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` (and `include_granted_scopes=true` if you add scopes step by step).
Make sure both scopes are listed on the OAuth consent screen in Cloud Console. To confirm, check the token's `scope` field at the tokeninfo endpoint.
